newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar rises vs mark in Tokyo after French vote.
newsitem.headline: Dollar rises vs mark in Tokyo after French vote.

text.p: 0300 GMT TRADED HI/LO AS OF 0300 GMT

The dollar powered higher against the mark by midday Tokyo on Monday as the Socialist-led opposition's win in Sunday's French election led to concerns about an enlarged EMU membership and a weak euro, dealers said.
The dollar came off its earlier highs on talk of sales by hedge funds and the Bank of France at 1.7150 marks, but it was likely to benefit as a safe haven amid uncertanity in Europe.
"Both domestic and overseas operators, including speculators, flocked to sell marks in morning trade after the results of the French election," said a German bank dealer.
"The dollar would be the best currency to buy against the mark and other European currencies," he added.
The result of the French parliamentary election was a major defeat for President Jacques Chirac's centre-right coalition, which lost almost half the 464 seats it held in the outgoing lower house.
The combined left won an absolute majority of at least 289 seats in France's parliamentary election on Sunday.

Just 40 minutes after polling stations closed, conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe went on television to concede defeat. The Socialist Party is committed to launching a single European currency, but is demanding a flexible interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty, a European "economic government" and early membership for Italy, Spain and Portugal in EMU.

"Tokyo operators mainly sold marks against the yen in cross trade as uncertainty grew in Europe," said a French bank dealer. He said sterling could rise against the mark due to speculation on higher U.K. interest rates and perceptions that it will not join in the first round of the single currency.
He and other dealers said there was talk that the Bank of France sold marks against the French franc around 3.3800 in Asian trade. The franc was at 3.3820/25 per mark at 0320 GMT.
The mark traded around 67.85 yen at 0331 GMT, down from 68.18 yen in late New York trade on Friday.

Stop-loss dollar buying against the mark was triggered at several points, including 1.7110 and 1.7130 marks. Further stop-loss buying is expected at 1.7185 marks, said the German bank dealer in Tokyo. "A dollar rise above 1.7185 marks may be overdone in the near term, although it could strengthen over the long term," he added.

There has been speculation that the Bundesbank may bow to political pressure to revalue its gold reserves in a bid to clear hurdles for joining the euro, and this also prompted mark sales, dealers said. A German newspaper reported on Sunday that, in private talks with the Bonn government since January, Bundesbank officials have not opposed a plan to revalue the central bank's gold and currency reserves.

In the dollar/yen arena, there was little impetus to move out of recent trading ranges, although investor bids were seen below 116 yen. The dollar closed around 116.30 yen in New York on Friday. --Tatsuo Ito 81-3-3432-1396
